facts.statement: Paratypothorax is an extinct genus of aetosaur that contains only one known species, Paratypothorax andressorum.
facts.quote: Paratypothorax is an extinct genus of aetosaur, known from a single species, Paratypothorax andressorum.

facts.statement: Paratypothorax was a widely distributed aetosaur found in Germany, North America, and possibly parts of Gondwana.
facts.quote: It was a broadly distributed member of the group found in Germany, North America, and possibly parts of Gondwana.

facts.statement: The best specimens of Paratypothorax come from Germany, but for over a century they were incorrectly identified as phytosaur armor.
facts.quote: The best specimens come from Germany, though for more than a century they were mistakenly considered phytosaur armor.

facts.statement: Paratypothorax was first discovered from specimens collected in the Heslach area near Stuttgart, Germany.
facts.quote: Paratypothorax was first known from specimens collected from the Heslach area near Stuttgart in Germany.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Paratypothorax, SMNS 5721, consists of articulated osteoderms along with some hip and leg bones.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of Paratypothorax, SMNS 5721, consists of a series of articulated osteoderms alongside a few hip and leg bones.

facts.statement: Paratypothorax was first recognized as an aetosaur in 1953 and was formally named as a new genus in 1985.
facts.quote: Paratypothorax was first recognized as an aetosaur in 1953, and was named as a new genus in 1985.

facts.statement: Fossils of Paratypothorax were first identified in the Chinle Group of the southwestern United States in 1992.
facts.quote: In 1992, Paratypothorax fossils were first identified in the Chinle Group of the southwestern United States.

facts.statement: Paratypothorax fossils have been found in the Sonsela Member of Petrified Forest National Park in Arizona and the Bluewater Creek Formation in western New Mexico.
facts.quote: It has been found in the Sonsela Member of Petrified Forest National Park in Arizona, as well as the Bluewater Creek Formation of western New Mexico.

facts.statement: Osteoderms of Paratypothorax have been reported from the Norian-age Fleming Fjord Formation in Greenland, the Zarzaitine Series in Algeria, and an unverified site in India.
facts.quote: Osteoderms of Paratypothorax have also been reported from the Norian-age Fleming Fjord Formation in Greenland, the Zarzaitine Series of Algeria, and an unverified occurrence in India.

facts.statement: Paratypothorax has wide, strap-like paramedian scutes featuring grooves and pits that create radial patterns.
facts.quote: Paratypothorax possesses paramedian scutes that are wide, strap-like, and have grooves and pits on them forming radial patterns.

facts.statement: The lateral scutes of Paratypothorax bear large horns that curve backward, a trait shared with other typothoracisines like Typothorax.
facts.quote: Like other typothoracisines such as Typothorax, the lateral scutes bear large horns that are posteriorly hooked.

facts.statement: The rear of each scute on Paratypothorax is overlapped by a prominent knob.
facts.quote: The rear of each scute is overlapped by a prominent knob.

facts.statement: Paratypothorax was a large, wide-bodied typothoracine aetosaur and serves as the namesake for the tribe Paratypothoracisini.
facts.quote: Paratypothorax was a large and wide-bodied typothoracine aetosaur, as well as the namesake of the tribe Paratypothoracisini.

facts.statement: Paratypothorax is classified within the family Stagonolepididae.
Paratypothorax belongs to the tribe Paratypothoracisini.
The fossil range of Paratypothorax is estimated to be from the Late Carnian to the Rhaetian.
The formations in the southwestern United States where Paratypothorax was found date to the Carnian and Rhaetian stages of the Late Triassic.

facts.statement: Paratypothorax lived during the Norian stage, approximately 227.3 to 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: A complete skeleton of Paratypothorax, specimen SMNS 19003, was unearthed in 1945 from the Schlipf Quarry near Murrhardt.
facts.quote: Among this formerly misidentified material is SMNS 19003, a fossil unearthed in 1945 from the Schlipf Quarry near Murrhardt.
